requirements.quote: In your personal shell start-up file `/home/user/.bashrc`, the *last* two non-blank, non-comment lines must be **exactly**:
there must be no spaces before “export” and each line must end with a single newline character “\n”.

check.cmd: [ "$(tail -c1 /home/user/.bashrc | od -An -c | tr -d ' ')" = '\n' ] && grep -qx 'export TZ="Etc/UTC"' /home/user/.bashrc && grep -qx 'export LANG="en_US.UTF-8"' /home/user/.bashrc

requirements.quote: A new shell spawned after the task produces `Etc/UTC` from `echo $TZ` and `en_US.UTF-8` from `echo $LANG`.
The file **must contain exactly three lines, in this precise order, with no leading/trailing blanks on any line**:
File permissions must allow read access to everyone (i.e. mode 644 or more permissive).
One more thing: `/var/lib/zephyr` is no longer wanted on this host, so remove it and all of its contents.
